candidates.title: Computational material scientist / DFT expert
candidates.desc: We are seeking an expert in computational materials science to help discover the next generation of breakthrough materials. You will work in a small, highly interdisciplinary team of DFT/AI/materials experts and develop and execute end-to-end workflows for identifying, ranking, and de-risking candidate materials. You will collaborate closely with our synthesis and characterization team to translate predictions into experiments, improve models with real-world feedback, and build a closed-loop discovery engine. While there is an opportunity to publish selected results, our overarching goal is to deliver new, high-impact materials that can be validated experimentally and ultimately scaled. This role combines scientific depth with teamwork and execution ownership. You will contribute to strategic decisions on methodology, prioritization, and platform direction. You will receive a competitive compensation package with possible equity participation. Key responsibilities Materials discovery & scientific leadership Design, implement, and continuously improve DFT-based workflows to predict key functional properties of crystalline materials. Develop screening strategies and decision criteria to down-select candidates from large search spaces and guide experimental validation. Own the computational plan for assigned discovery programs: define milestones, success criteria, and deliverables; drive execution. Automation and experimental collaboration Build robust, automated, and reproducible DFT pipelines. Improve throughput via AI/ML workflow optimization. Maintain high-quality documentation, versioned workflows, and traceable datasets. Work with synthesis/characterization colleagues to interpret results, troubleshoot discrepancies, and incorporate learnings into improved workflows. Communication & impact Communicate results clearly to both computational and experimental teammates (written summaries, internal presentations). Where appropriate, contribute to publications, conference abstracts, and grant/partner materials (without compromising IP strategy). Required qualifications PhD in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a closely related field. Deep hands-on experience in DFT on crystalline materials (4+ years), evidenced by strong publications and/or impactful open work. Demonstrated experience with automation and acceleration of DFT (workflows, convergence optimization, error handling, high-throughput screening). Experience applying AI/ML methods for materials discovery and search. Strong programming skills in Python (or similar) and familiarity with scientific software practices (version control, testing, reproducibility). Comfortable working in a fast-moving startup environment: pragmatic prioritization, ownership, strong collaboration. DFT + methods Experience with one or more of: VASP, Quantum ESPRESSO, GPAW, ABINIT, WIEN2k, CASTEP (or comparable codes). candidates.title: Magnet Scientist
candidates.desc: We are seeking an ambitious Magnet Scientist to lead the fabrication and engineering of next-generation magnetic materials. This is a lab-first, execution-driven role where you will go beyond composition discovery to engineer the microstructure, processing routes, and ultimate performance of AI-predicted materials. You will bridge the gap between computational predictions and physical reality, turning promising alloys into high-performance magnets by controlling phase formation, grain structure, and defects. Key Responsibilities Microstructure Engineering & Fabrication Execute day-to-day experimental synthesis using physical vapor deposition, melt growth, flux growth, and arc-melting. Design advanced heat treatments, annealing profiles, and processing routes to control grain size, texture, and phase distribution. Engineer coercivity, remanence, and temperature stability through precise microstructure design. Develop scale-up routes from ingot to powder to bulk magnets, including sintering or hot pressing. Characterization & Physics Perform high-level X-ray structure determination and spectroscopy. Measure hysteresis loops and temperature-dependent properties using magnetometry (VSM/PPMS or equivalent). Analyze domain behavior, reversal mechanisms, and magnetic anisotropy to provide physics-driven feedback to the AI team. Required qualifications PhD or MSc in Physics, Materials Science, Metallurgy, or Chemistry with 5+ years of hands-on experience. Expertise in the synthesis and fabrication of inorganic crystals, specifically permanent magnets or functional intermetallics. Demonstrated experience in Microstructure Design and studying structure-property relationships. Proficiency in magnetic characterization using PPMS or VSM systems. Preferred qualifications Experience with rare-earth or rare-earth-free magnets and powder metallurgy. Familiarity with EBSD, SEM, TEM for detailed microstructure analysis. Experience generating data for patents and industrial qualification.

candidates.title: Materials Scientist
candidates.desc: We are seeking hands-on Research Scientists to execute day-to-day experimental synthesis and characterization of AI-predicted materials. You will work directly with the Head of Materials Synthesis & Characterization and computational team to rapidly translate AI materials predictions into physical samples and high-quality characterization data. This is a lab-first, execution-driven role with strong ownership of experimental results and direct contribution to cutting edge AI-enable workflow and feedback loop, IP generation and industrial validation. We look for ambitious candidates with passion and perseverance, and for good team players. The ideal candidate is an independent problem solver, someone who likes to make new things, and has the grit necessary to make things work. You will be part of an agile and growing team, pushing boundaries for progress and discoveries with a competitive compensation package including equity participation. You should have a material synthesis expert with a background in condensed matter physics, inorganic chemistry, or material science. You should have expertise in a few of the following synthesis techniques: physical vapor deposition, melt-growth, flux-growth, and arc-melting. You should be familiar with X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy, electron microscopy, and elemental analysis, as well as PPMS (or similar) methods. You should have a high level of experimental rigor and documentation discipline. Required Qualifications PhD or MSc in physics, chemistry, or material science with 5+ years of hands-on experience Expertise in the synthesis of inorganic crystals, e.g. permanent magnets, van der Waals materials, superconductors, Perovskite compounds, Kondo topological fermions, cubic and hexagonal Laves compounds, etc. Expertise in characterization of new materials using X-ray structure determination, SEM-EDS Expertise in characterization of new materials using cryogenic transport and magnetization measurements (e.g., PPMS, VSM) Ability to quickly learn different growth methods Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of different low-temperature materials characterization methods Experience with magnets Familiarity with automation and lab data management Experience in generating data for patents or industrial qualifications

candidates.title: PhD PhD: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Semiconductor Metrology View position
candidates.desc: PhD: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Semiconductor Metrology - ARCNL Careers Repository Candidate portal Search PhD: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Semiconductor Metrology Work Activities How can we combine machine learning and physics to recover nanoscale information from imperfect images? Modern computer chips are built with features only a few nanometers across, yet manufacturers need to measure these structures with extraordinary precision and do so quickly enough to keep up with large-scale production. This creates a fascinating computational challenge: how can we infer hidden physical properties from limited, noisy, and low-resolution measurement data? In this project, you will develop a novel physics-informed machine learning approach that integrates physical simulations of the measurement process with its inverse reconstruction. A key challenge is the data-driven design of the experimental setup: exploring how the choice of measurements and configurations can be optimized to extract the most useful information for reliable parameter reconstruction. You will work in close collaboration with the research department at ASML, the Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI, Prof. dr. Tristan van Leeuwen), and the AI4Science Lab, Informatics Institute, University of Amsterdam (dr. Patrick Forré), combining industrial relevance with academic depth in computational science and mathematical modeling. Qualifications You have (or soon will have) a MSc degree in computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, applied mathematics, physics, or a related discipline, meeting the Dutch university requirements for entry into a PhD program. A background in machine learning, inverse problems, scientific computing, or related data-driven methods is highly desirable. You are curious about combining physical modeling with data-driven methods and are motivated to work at the interface of academia and industry. Strong analytical skills, a collaborative mindset, and proficiency in verbal and written English are essential. Work environment ARCNL performs fundamental research, focusing on the physics and chemistry involved in current and future key technologies in nanolithography, primarily for the semiconductor industry. While the academic setting and research style are geared towards establishing scientific excellence, the topics in ARCNL’s research program are intimately connected with the interests of the industrial partner ASML. The institute is located at Amsterdam Science Park and currently employs about 100 persons of which 65 are ambitious (young) researchers from all over the globe. www.arcnl.nl Working conditions The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment in the service of the Netherlands Foundation of Scientific Research Institutes (NWO-I) for the duration of four years, with a starting salary of gross € 3.115 per month and a range of employment benefits . With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving. But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world. Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential. HVM Senior Field Process Engineer – tALD, PEALD, LPCVD As part of the Global Sales and Services business unit, our Field Process Engineering team consists of on-site process application experts focused on improving process performance and stability on ASM toolsets at customer locations. In this role, you will support Thermal Atomic Layer Deposition (tALD), Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition (PEALD), or Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) on ASM’s XP8 DCM/QCM or SONORA platforms. You will optimize deposition processes, resolve technical issues, and ensure tool performance meets customer and ASM requirements. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy hands‑on problem‑solving, fast‑paced environments, and contributing to next‑generation semiconductor manufacturing. The Field Process Engineer serves as a key technical interface with the customer and must demonstrate accountability, professionalism, and clear communication. Engineers in this role often transition into technical leadership, customer strategy, or product development roles. You’ll collaborate with ASM’s global innovation teams and have access to advanced R&D resources. What you'll be working on Lead on-site process qualification and optimization during tool installations and ramp‑up. Track and verify compliance with customer specifications throughout installation, ramp-up, and warranty phases. Design and execute experiments to improve film quality, uniformity, and throughput. Troubleshoot process issues using a systematic root cause analysis. Drive containment, short-term mitigation, and long-term corrective actions to resolve issues and restore process performance. Partner with customer teams and internal ASM teams to drive continuous improvement and tool‑to‑tool matching. Develop and maintain relevant technical documentation for internal and external stakeholders. Share lessons learned across the key account organization and the Global Sales and Services business unit. Customer Engagement Serve as the primary technical interface among customer process teams, hardware teams, and ASM account teams. Anticipate customer needs and provide sustainable, long-term solutions. Support escalations with clear communication, action plans, and disciplined follow‑through. Represent ASM with professionalism

You will design and conduct complex experiments, perform detailed data interpretation, and deliver robust processes that meet requirements for removal rate, uniformity, defectivity, planarity, and pattern-dependent performance (e.g., dishing/erosion). You will collaborate cross-functionally with R&D, product engineering, field/service, and customers to define requirements, execute demonstrations, and enable successful product adoption. While you deliver creative and inventive solutions, technical publications and Intellectual Property (IP) generation are an essential function of this position. Key Responsibilities Develop, qualify, and optimize CMP unit processes for FEOL/BEOL applications (e.g., SiC, STI, ILD, W, Cu, barrier/liner, low‑k, hardmask, advanced dielectrics) and advanced materials to balance planarity, selectivity, and defect control. Formulate and tune CMP consumables and process conditions, including slurry chemistry (oxidizers, complexing agents, corrosion inhibitors, pH control, abrasives, surfactants), pads, conditioners, and post-CMP clean chemistries to meet performance and yield targets. Drive improvements in critical CMP outputs including removal rate (RR), within-wafer non-uniformity (WIWNU), across-wafer uniformity, edge performance, dishing/erosion, scratch/particle levels, residue control, and corrosion mitigation. Design and conduct experiments using structured tools such as Design of Experiments (DOE) and Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to achieve stated objectives. Perform rigorous analysis of complex experimental output (e.g., RR maps, thickness/step height measurements, defect Pareto, metrology correlation, pattern density impacts, consumable aging effects). candidates.desc:
Your Role

As a Defect Inspection Engineer/Expert, you will be responsible for ensuring the defect-free quality of semiconductor wafers using Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) systems and unpatterned wafer inspection.

You will detect defects such as particles, scratches, haze, and surface roughness that could impact the yield of our integrated graphene photonics process flow. Working in a cleanroom environment, you will collaborate with process, equipment and integration teams to set up, qualify and optimize inspection recipes, troubleshoot issues, and continuously improve defect detection and classification.

What You’ll Do

 - Perform AOI and unpatterned wafer inspection on materials such as bare silicon, epitaxial layers and polished wafers

 - Set up, qualify and optimize inspection recipes

 - Fine-tune inspection tool and recipe parameters to improve defect-detection sensitivity, inspection quality, repeatability and overall performance

 - Analyze defect data to identify trends, root causes and potential process excursions

 - Interpret defect data and translate findings into actionable insights for process teams

 - Generate defect maps, Pareto charts and reports to communicate findings

 - Participate in Design of Experiments (DOE) to optimize inspection parameters

 - Troubleshoot inspection-related issues and support continuous improvement in defect detection and classification

 - Collaborate with process, equipment and integration teams

What You Bring

 - A bachelor’s degree or above in electrical engineering, materials science, physics or a related field

 - 5+ years of experience in semiconductor inspection, with a focus on AOI and unpatterned wafer inspection

 - Hands-on experience with unpatterned wafer inspection systems, such as SPx, and AOI tools such as Eagle or Dragonfly

 - Understanding of semiconductor process flows, including polishing, epitaxy and cleaning

 - Familiarity with defect classification, SEM review and Statistical Process Control (SPC)

 - Proficiency in AOI and defect-review software, such as KLA Klarity and Camtek Inspecta

 - Ability to optimize inspection tools and recipe parameters for sensitivity, inspection quality and repeatability

 - Ability to interpret defect data and identify relevant trends and improvement opportunities

 - Proficiency in JMP for statistical analysis, data visualization and DOE

 - Familiarity with MATLAB or Python is an advantage

 - Excellent communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate across functions

What We Offer

 - The opportunity to work on defect inspection for an integrated graphene photonics process flow

 - A cleanroom-based role with close collaboration across process, equipment and integration teams

candidates.desc:
About us

We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects

About our technology

The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude  
 
In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution



The Role

We are seeking an experienced Electronic-Photonics IC Mask Data Preparation & GDS Data Integration Engineer to take technical ownership of the complete tape-out flow — from GDS database integration and mask data preparation through mask release, first silicon bring-up, and post-tapeout support. 

In this role, you will drive EIC+PIC DfX co-integration (Design for Functionality, Manufacturing, Test, Packaging, and Reliability) across a 300 mm graphene photonics platform, ensuring seamless alignment between design, fabrication, testing, and packaging requirements throughout the development cycle.

To join our team, you should be excited to:

As a Defect Inspection Engineer/Expert, you will be responsible for ensuring the defect-free quality of semiconductor wafers using Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) systems and unpatterned wafer inspection.

candidates.title: Expert Robotics AI (f/m/div.)
candidates.desc: As part of our team, you will own the robotics AI architecture and technical hypotheses, selecting world-action and video-action models, VLA policies, embodied reasoning, or classical planning according to task, data, and execution constraints. You will design heterogeneous systems that connect learned models with Code-as-Policy programs, Graph-as-Policy structures, and reusable skills. You specify state and action representations, interfaces, execution checks, as well as recovery behavior. Additionally, you will implement and adapt models and agentic robot programs. You investigate predictive dynamics, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or feedback-driven skill refinement, then justify your choices with baselines and ablations. You will also define evaluation across simulation and physical rollouts, including held-out tasks, embodiment transfer, intervention rate, latency, recovery, and repeatability. In doing so, you distinguish first-attempt success from results achieved through retries. Furthermore, you will collaborate closely with the deployment engineer to turn the architecture into a functioning embodiment. Together, you diagnose model, planning, or control failures and revise the design based on measured robot behavior. candidates.title: Materials Informatics Scientist (Evaluation-focused)
candidates.desc: Define how AI models for materials discovery are evaluated, compared, and trusted Dunia is building AI for one of the hardest unsolved problems in science: turning materials discovery from an academic, trial-and-error process into a programmable, scalable discipline. As our models grow more complex and our experimental throughput increases, the limiting factor is no longer generating predictions, but knowing which ones to believe. As Materials Informatics Scientist (Evaluation-focused), you will own the evaluation and validation of AI models applied to materials discovery. Your role is to ensure that model performance claims are meaningful, comparable, and decision-relevant, and that progress in AI for Materials reflects real improvements in discovery, not artifacts of metrics or datasets. This role is not about building new models. It is about defining the standards by which models are judged. Your tasks will include: Own evaluation as a scientific discipline Design, implement, and maintain evaluation frameworks for AI models across materials discovery tasks Define metrics and protocols that reflect generalization, robustness, uncertainty, and experimental relevance Identify failure modes, dataset leakage, and misleading performance signals Interrogate and compare models Systematically benchmark different model classes, training regimes, and representations Evaluate tradeoffs between accuracy, uncertainty, data efficiency, and usability Provide clear, defensible recommendations on which models to trust, deploy, or retire Connect AI performance to real outcomes Link model behavior to experimental results and program-level objectives Distinguish improvements that change decisions from those that only improve abstract scores Help research and programs teams understand what current models can and cannot reliably do Build robust analytical tooling Develop and maintain professional-grade scripts and analysis pipelines for evaluation and benchmarking Visualize complex, high-dimensional results in ways that surface real insight Ensure disciplined, reproducible handling of data, code, and results Communicate truth clearly Present findings clearly to AI researchers, materials scientists, and leadership Produce concise summaries that align the organization around a shared view of evidence and uncertainty Act as an independent scientific reference point when claims require validation PhD (strongly preferred) or Master’s degree in materials science, chemistry, physics, machine learning, or a related field Significant experien ce (typically 5–8 years ) working with scientific or ML systems under real-world uncertainty Demonstrated experience evaluating, benchmarking, or validating models rather than only building them Strong programming skills in Python and scientific data tooling Deep appreciation for rigor, reproducibility, and careful interpretation of results English fluency, additional languages preferred

We are aware that women often face particular challenges in their professional lives - whether due to unconscious bias, the compatibility of career and care work or structural barriers. We therefore take targeted measures to actively promote equal opportunities in the application process. Facts and figures Statistics on applications from 2024 show that although only 34 % of applications were from women, women made up 54 % of those applicants who were invited to interviews. Women also make up a disproportionately high share of new recruits, accounting for 41% of new employees. These figures show how women are not discriminated against in our application process. On the contrary, as a woman, you have a good chance of being invited to interview and ultimately being recruited at Forschungszentrum Jülich. Gender equality and gender diversity are integral parts of Forschungszentrum Jülich’s values and objectives. The Gender Equality Plan contains further information on the measures taken in the area of recruitment and on achieving gender balance in leadership positions. Job advertisements Job requirements : Studies show that women are more likely to apply for a job only if they meet almost all of the requirements. This is why we would particularly encourage women applicants to apply for a position if the job description appeals to them, even if they do not meet 100 % of the requirements. Wording : Our gender-neutral job advertisements are reviewed and revised by our recruiting team before publication to ensure that the wording used is appropriate and appeals to women in particular. Diversity statement : “We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, e.g. in terms of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation / identity, and social, ethnic and religious origin. A diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities in which everyone can realize their potential is important to us.” You will find this diversity statement in all our job advertisements – we aim to continuously promote diversity among our employees! Selection process Overview of the application process The selection process may include a short video interview as part of a pre-selection round and will always consist of an in-depth interview (virtual or on site). Interviews at Forschungszentrum Jülich are conducted on an equal footing and are intended to help both sides reach a decision. We partner closely with our customers to deliver differentiated, power-efficient, high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. At GF, you'll find the opportunity to make an impact, work with world-class talent and contribute to a more secure, sustainable future. Your Job In semiconductor manufacturing, no processing machine runs continuously yielding the same results. Materials used in the machine can degrade over time, simple factors like –outside temperature can fluctuate, and high usage and low usage play a roll. For stable process results, specific machine settings and recipe parameters are tuned automatically or manually. This is an essential part of work for our process and equipment experts. As a PhD candidate, you will be looking differently at our machines and processes. You already have a scientist´s or an engineer´s view. candidates.title: Metrology Engineer 3
candidates.desc: The group you’ll be a part of In the Global Products Group, we are dedicated to excellence in the design and engineering of Lam's etch and deposition products. We drive innovation to ensure our cutting-edge solutions are helping to solve the biggest challenges in the semiconductor industry. The impact you’ll make At Lam, as a Metrology Engineer, you will help develop next-generation on-tool metrology and sensing technologies that enable smarter semiconductor manufacturing. Working at the intersection of semiconductor processes, optical sensing, machine vision, spectroscopy, and data analytics, you will transform raw sensor data into actionable process insights that improve equipment performance, productivity, and wafer outcomes. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, software, process technology, and data science teams to develop measurement solutions capable of quantifying wafer characteristics directly on semiconductor processing equipment. Through hands-on experimentation, data analysis, and model development, you will help accelerate the transition from concept to product deployment for emerging Equipment Intelligence technologies. In this role, you will directly contribute to the development and deployment of vision- and spectroscopy-based metrology systems that enable real-time characterization of film thickness, uniformity, defectivity, process drift, and other critical wafer-level measurements. What you’ll do Develop and deploy spectroscopy-, imaging-, and vision-based metrology systems for non-contact wafer characterization, including film thickness, uniformity, defect detection, process monitoring, and equipment health assessment. Design and execute experiments to characterize sensor performance, quantify measurement uncertainty, evaluate sensitivity, and perform MSA, Gauge R&R, capability, and error-budget analyses. Develop calibration methods, measurement models, and analytics that transform optical, spectral, image, and equipment signals into actionable metrics for monitoring, diagnostics, optimization, and process control. candidates.title: Process Engineer 3
candidates.desc: About the role: Lam Research is seeking a highly motivated Process Engineer 3 (PE3) to join the Global Metrology Team. The successful candidate will drive the development and implementation of advanced in-situ and analytical metrology solutions to accelerate process understanding, improve on-wafer performance, and support the development of low global warming potential (GWP) process technologies with reduced carbon footprint. The engineer will lead the application of in-situ diagnostic techniques including GP-FTIR, FTIR, Mass Spectrometry (MS), UV-Vis, Raman spectroscopy, and related technologies to establish mechanistic understanding of complex process interactions and enable next-generation process control strategies. What you’ll do ESCs are a highly multidisciplinary technology and offer the opportunity to innovate at the intersection of physics, materials, and software algorithms to provide our customers with differentiated solutions. Lam etch customers continue to tighten requirements on defectivity, process window, and uniformity to meet the needs of ever-shrinking device dimensions. Electrostatic chucks are at the forefront of these needs, as thermal uniformity, voltage process window, and, to a large extent, defectivity limits are defined by this piece of hardware. Lam is continually improving ESC performance in all of these areas to meet customer needs. Understanding the performance of this particular part of Lam plasma etchers requires a multidisciplinary background, incorporating elements of materials science, physics, and mechanical and electrical engineering to fully understand the implications of design changes on customer processing. At Lila, the data is generated for the model: we run our own experiments at scale, and you will help decide what gets measured. The question is not only what to learn from a fixed dataset, but what datasets should exist. And model outputs are reasoned over. Predictions go to systems and scientists choosing what to run next and making mechanistic calls downstream. Both need to know why, not only what. A model that returns a quantity a biologist, human or AI, can argue with; models that transfer to new contexts, compose into a downstream calculation, and can be checked against an independent measurement are often worth more than a more accurate one that returns an embedding. What You'll Be Building Build domain models for perturbation, genetic, and multimodal experimental data, and translate biological questions into rigorous ML problem formulations. Where the biology supports it, build models with interpretable structure — representations grounded in the machinery that executes a biological process rather than in cell-type identity embeddings, and parameters a biologist can argue with. Make uncertainty a deliverable. Calibrated posteriors, honest error bars, and outputs that tell a downstream consumer how much a prediction can actually settle — particularly when predicting into conditions never measured. Pre-register and beat baselines. Simple entity-mean, additive, and linear baselines are stated before any model is fit. If the full model does not beat them, we ship the baseline and say so. Partner with experimental scientists to guide data generation and model validation — shaping what gets measured, in what contexts, at what precision — and build the experiment-selection methods that choose the next batch of measurements to reduce uncertainty where it matters. candidates.title: Senior Lithography and Process Development Engineer
candidates.desc: Join Mycronic's Pattern Generators Division as a Senior Lithography & Process Development Engineer and play a key role in developing lithography processes for advanced semiconductor and display manufacturing. As part of the Metrology and Process Control group (PMCD), you will be responsible for driving process excellence through advanced process control, technology development, and continuous improvement. You will ensure robust, capable, and stable lithography processes while contributing to the development of future manufacturing technologies.

candidates.title: Field Application Engineer
candidates.desc: Position Overview As a Field Application Engineer, you will play a critical role in bridging Nearfield Instruments’ technology, customers, and internal development teams. Based at our client site in Leuven, Belgium, you will support the successful deployment and application of Nearfield’s advanced Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) solutions within a leading semiconductor R&D environment. You will work closely with customer engineers and researchers to address complex metrology challenges, demonstrate system performance, and translate customer requirements into future product and application developments. As a highly customer-facing technical expert, you will act as a key liaison between our client, R&D, Product Management, Engineering, and Commercial teams, helping ensure that Nearfield’s next-generation metrology solutions continue to meet the evolving needs of the semiconductor industry. Why This Role Is Important The semiconductor industry continues to push the limits of device scaling and complexity. As traditional metrology approaches face increasing challenges, advanced AFM-based metrology is becoming essential for enabling accurate process control at the nanoscale. As a Field Application Engineer, you will help drive the adoption and success of Nearfield’s breakthrough metrology technology within one of the world's most advanced semiconductor research environments. Your work will directly contribute to the development of next-generation semiconductor. Key Responsibilities Customer Application Support & Technical Engagement Demonstrate the capabilities of our AFM systems on customer wafers and evaluate application performance. Identify and understand customer metrology challenges and process control requirements. Analyse measurement data and translate findings into clear recommendations and actionable insights. Present technical results and showcase the unique value of Nearfield Instruments' solutions to customers. Develop and optimize measurement recipes for advanced semiconductor applications. Lead investigations into measurement and data-processing related issues and coordinate resolution with support, engineering, and development teams. Work with Development & Engineering and R&D teams to create new metrology solutions, measurement modes, algorithms, and data analysis capabilities. Capture customer feedback, technology roadmaps, and future requirements to help shape the next generation of products. What We Offer A high-impact role in a fast-growing deep-tech company Opportunity to contribute to Nearfield’s growth in a strategic market Strong collaboration with international teams Learning and development in a global commercial environment A dynamic and entrepreneurial working environment Location Leuven, Belgium (Onsite) 9:00–17:00 Flexible working hours available Overtime may be required Five-day workweek, with weekends and public holidays off Business trip to our HQ in Rotterdam or other clients’ sites are quired About Nearfield Instrumen

candidates.title: Field Applications Engineer- Taiwan
candidates.desc: At Nearfield Instruments we're looking for a Field Applications Engineer Hsinchu, Taiwan to join our team. Meet the complex metrology needs of the semiconductor industry in this customer-facing role at a rapidly growing scale-up. Chips are shrinking, becoming increasingly powerful and complex. But as a result, currently used metrology systems in the semiconductor industry no longer meet process control requirements. Nearfield Instruments offers the solution in terms of speed, precision and the capability of measuring the very latest, most complex 3D nanostructures. As a metrology application engineer, you will play a key role in identifying and meeting each customer’s metrology needs. Would you like to collaborate with the world’s leading chipmakers and get to see the results of your work in practice? We’re growing hiring. What you’re going to do? In your role, you will help the customer get the most out of our products and represent the voice of the customer towards to the central teams. You will assist the world’s leading chipmakers stay in control of their manufacturing processes by demonstrating the capabilities of our cutting-edge atomic force microscopy (AFM) systems on customer wafers. Your input will also contribute to R&D to meet future needs of our customers. The simulations will involve complex and irreversible systems, where early choices constrain later ones and outcomes are delayed. Distribution-free statistical theory and metrological discipline will be directly integrated into the evaluation of black-box deep learning architectures. The main goal is to design independent statistical oversight layers to monitor AI behavior and catch systemic errors under dataset shift. Specifically, the research will target two major AI failure modes: 1) Silent Overconfidence : This occurs when an AI operates on shifted out-of-distribution data but continues to output incorrect predictions with high mathematical certainty. You will design and evaluate distribution-free calibration and uncertainty quantification (UQ) frameworks to force deep architectures to output honest, mathematically guaranteed coverage intervals. 2) Rapid Failure Velocity : Because automated systems execute instantly, a mis-calibrated AI agent can propagate a continuous string of systematic errors at runtime speed before human operators can intervene. You will develop independent tracking layers using advanced time series and multivariate monitoring methods to isolate small, sustained process drifts before they hit catastrophic boundaries. Duties Conduct a comprehensive survey of state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification methods for AI models and tools, and software implementation of these methods. Develop test examples for evaluating their performance, conduct relevant simulation experiments, and publish the results. Construct a parameterized, mathematical Python testbed simulating a multistage sequential decision framework (inspired by manufacturing workflows) characterized by time-delays, irreversibility, and endogenous data generation loops (i.e., Abstract Process Simulation). Develop functional, lightweight AI agent architectures to interact with the simulated environment, establishing a controlled subject for statistical stress testing (i.e., Agent-Environment Implementation). This is a hybrid research and infrastructure role. Roughly half your time will be spent working directly with our experimental and computational scientists, building agents and tools that solve active research problems. This role requires domain depth, not just data engineering skill. You need to know, for example, what metadata actually matters for a given characterization technique. The work demands attention to detail and a willingness to get into the weeds: to meticulously read, understand, and improve our data. You'll be as much a materials scientist doing research as the person who makes our agentic harness actually work.



What You'll Do

 - Work directly with lab scientists and the computational team on active research problems, staying close to the actual bottlenecks LLM agents are meant to solve.

 - Investigate agent traces to identify data errors and agentic failure modes, and eliminate them at the source.

 - Restructure and re-architect our materials databases (lab experiments, characterization data, computations) around how LLM agents actually reason and fail, not just around human readability. Draw on domain expertise about how to represent the data and what metadata matters.

 - Work with the hardware and automation teams to make data collection more robust.

 - Build research software for lab environments, translating scientific requirements into working tools.

 - Distill what you learn into evaluations that measure agent performance.

At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary A CMP (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) Process Engineer is responsible for the critical semiconductor manufacturing step of planarizing the wafer surface. This is achieved through a synergistic combination of chemical reactions and mechanical force, ensuring that subsequent layers of the chip can be built with high precision. The primary goal of a CMP engineer is to achieve a flat wafer surface by controlling the chemical reaction and mechanical force. Role and Responsibilities Here's What You'll Be Responsible For: Removal Rate (RR) Control: Conducting performance evaluations of various influence factors to ensure the thickness skew before and after CMP is consistent across the entire wafer. Condition Optimization: Determining the optimal process conditions to improve uniformity and resolve chronic issues, such as "center low RR profiles. Recipe Management: Developing and optimizing Recipe (RCP) parameters and improve flatness. Defect & uniformity Management: Managing and improving wafer uniformity and resolving defects such as scratches and particles. Consumable Life Cycle Management: Monitoring the usage cycles of consumables (pads, slurry) to ensure they do not exceed specifications, which could impact quality. Material Evaluation: Evaluating the performance of different slurries and polishing pads to optimize the CMP process. Skills and Qualifications Here's What You'll Need: Basic requirement BS or MS in Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Material Science, or Computer Science. A minimum 5 years of related experience; Semiconductor Process Flows. Previous experience in a high-volume semiconductor manufacturing environment desired. Applicable manufacturing experience in other industries can be considered. Basic CMP Knowledge: Understanding of dielectric and metal CMP fundamentals, including slurry-pad-conditioning interactions and post-clean steps. Prefer to have some level of Equipment Familiarities: Hands-on experience with major industry CMP tools: AMAT/EBara and their end point systems Data & Statistics: Proficiency in Statistical Process Control (SPC), Fault Detection and Classification (FDC), and analysis software like JMP or Spotfire. Problem Solving: Ability to drive root-cause analysis using methodologies like FMEA, 8D, and first-principles physics approaches. Flexibility: As per business needs, sometimes it is required to work during off-hour times and/or with CWW shift schedule. This involves defining the long-term yield roadmap, establishing key performance indicators (KPIs), and leading high-priority task forces to resolve critical production risks. Furthermore, the position is responsible for mentoring junior engineers and interfacing with executive leadership to provide transparent insights into the health and risks of the fabrication process. Partner with Module and Process Integration engineers to solve complex critical defect issues. Support technology launch, ramp, and transfer across nodes and fab. Collaborate with Design and Product teams to ensure manufacturability and resolve layout-dependent yield issues before mass production ramp. Drive containment and corrective actions

candidates.title: Experienced Module Integration Engineer
candidates.desc: About Samsung Austin Semiconductor Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary We are seeking a motivated and high-caliber Module Integration Engineer to join our 2nm GAAFET team. This role focuses on the Front-End-of-Line (FEOL) integration, specifically targeting the RPMG (Replacement Metal Gate) and CTSDB (PC and NS isolation) modules. As we transition from FinFET to GAAFET (Gate-All-Around FET) architecture, you will play a critical role in bridging the gap between unit process development and overall device performance. You will work at the intersection of lithography, etch, deposition, and device physics to ensure the successful integration of the gate stack and contact modules for the next generation of computing. Role and Responsibilities Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For: Module Ownership: Support the integration and optimization of the RPMG and CTSDB modules to meet target device specifications for the 2nm node. Duties will require daily and consistent trend monitoring and quick responsive actions when needed. Process Integration: Collaborate with unit process engineers (Etch, CVD, ALD, CMP, Litho) to respond effectively to any module risks or issues related to process control and optimization. Characterization & Analysis: Execute and analyze DOE (Design of Experiments) to evaluate the impact of process variations on electrical performance. Failure Analysis: Understand advanced metrology and analysis data (TEM, SEM, AFM, EDX) for identify root causes of module failures and implement corrective actions. Data Management: Leverage statistical software (e.g., Cloud Data Sources, Spotfire, Python, etc.) to analyze large datasets and correlate process parameters with device yield. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Participate in design reviews and synchronization meetings with the Device and Layout teams to ensure manufacturability. Skills and Qualifications Here's what you'll need: Required Masters in Materials Science, Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Physics or a closely related field (industry experience can substitute for advanced degree). Preference for Ph.D. in Materials Science, Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Physics or a closely related field. · 2-3 years of relevant experience preferred, but not required for consideration. Knowledge of MOSFET Physics (GAAFET preferred but FinFET also desired): Deep understanding of device physics, especially for interfacial physics (gate oxide, threshold voltage control, gate capacitance, performance and reliability etc.) Process knowledge: Experience with or ability to understand various semiconductor process such as depositions (ALD/CVD), etch, and CMP, etc. Programming: Intermediate proficiency in Python, R, SQL for automating data extraction and visualization. candidates.desc: About Samsung Austin Semiconductor Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Yield and Process Control and Investigation(PCI) Engineer to join our semiconductor manufacturing team. In this role, you will be critical in monitoring wafer manufacturing processes, driving yield enhancement, and investigating process excursions. You will utilize advanced statistical process control (SPC), defect inspection data, and parametric testing results to identify root causes of yield limiters. Working closely with cross-functional teams—including Process, Equipment, and Integration engineering—you will implement robust solutions to ensure process stability, minimize defects, and maximize product yield. Role and Responsibilities Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For: Predictive Yield Modeling : Develop, implement, and validate complex yield prediction models that correlate inline metrology, defect inspection data and FDC(Fault Detection and Classification) metrics. Baseline Forecasting : Forecast yield trajectories for ramping and mature technology nodes, proactively identifying yield risk areas before wafers reach EDS test. Yield Analysis & Improvement: Drive end-to-end yield performance across wafer sort, parametric, and final tests by performing advanced data mining and statistical analysis to identify yield limiters and correlate detractors with electrical, inline, and defect data to implement improvement actions. Root Cause & Failure Analysis : Drive yield stability by leading root cause analysis through structured methodologies, correlating electrical signatures with physical defects via EFA/PFA partnerships, and collaborating with Design and Product teams to eliminate layout-dependent yield limiters before ramping. Data Science & Modeling: Apply advanced data science techniques and machine learning to build sophisticated yield models and automated analytics pipelines using Python, JMP, and SQL to enhance yield dataset analysis. Yield Management: Lead comprehensive yield management by defining strategic roadmaps, KPIs, and improvement strategies, while managing major yield excursions, mentoring junior engineers, and communicating yield health and risks to executive leadership. Skills and Qualifications Here's what you'll need: B.E. M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Applied Physics, or related field. Understanding of semiconductor device physics and CMOS fabrication processes (Lithography, Etch, Thin Films, CMP, Diffusion, Implant). Understanding of electrical parametric testing, defect inspection mechanisms. Strong technical writing and presentation skills to effectively communicate technical data to diverse audiences. candidates.employer_name: Toyota Research Institute (Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery)
candidates.title: Postdoctoral AI Fellow, Post-Training for Materials Discovery
candidates.desc:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.


The Team
The goal of TRI’s Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery (AMDD) program is to enable the materials breakthroughs needed for truly emissions-free mobility. We combine AI, autonomy, experimental data, and computational modeling to pursue a step change in the speed and scale of materials discovery. We collaborate closely with colleagues at universities, national labs, and global Toyota. Together, we develop capabilities designed for real-world impact in both Toyota’s industrial applications and open research more broadly.
The Opportunity
We are looking for a postdoctoral AI Fellow to define an original research direction in model post-training, using materials discovery as a real-world testbed. This appointment is anticipated to be for one year, with an option to extend another year by mutual agreement. You will take ownership of problem framing through validation and play a leading role in shaping the research as it evolves. No materials background is required, only the curiosity to learn from domain experts and uncover where AI can make a meaningful difference.
As part of AMDD, you will work closely with materials scientists, ML researchers, and software engineers to translate your ideas into capabilities that can inform real-world decisions. The fellowship is also intended to include an academic co-mentor in AI, with the specific collaboration developed with you after you join TRI, subject to institutional arrangements. Publications and conference presentations are encouraged and expected. Projects may also draw on internal datasets relevant to Toyota use cases. Ultimately, the goal is to pursue fundamental advances in AI while addressing important scientific and industrial challenges.

candidates.employer_name: Toyota Research Institute (Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery)
candidates.title: Postdoctoral Researcher, Human Aware Interaction Learning
candidates.desc:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.


The Opportunity
Our team at Toyota Research Institute is looking for a motivated and capable postdoc to conduct research on the computational and machine learning aspects of human-robot interaction. Areas of interest include applying foundation models to human-robot interaction, with an emphasis on understanding human-robot collaboration and how it evolves as foundation models become increasingly central to robotic manipulation. 
We’re looking for a postdoc with a solution driven attitude who can partner closely with our research team and turn ideas into impactful results. Relevant background topics include robot foundation models (e.g., VLAs, WAMs), imitation/reinforcement learning, leveraging language conditioning in trajectory planning/prediction, and decision-making under uncertainty, as well as human-machine teaming/shared control. 
The Challenge
In this project, we’re exploring novel approaches to efficiently learn how humans and robots collaborate. Our overall goal is to create AI approaches that challenge more traditional approaches to novel interactions with a human collaborator and enable the development of new embodied interactive policies. 
The project will be focused on researching a new approach in a specific sub-area of the overall goal, towards publications in top-tier conferences, well-matched for a postdoc that is looking for an additional year of research before beginning a faculty position, or a more experienced existing faculty member looking to take a year-long sabbatical with us. The fellowship will be in our Cambridge, MA research center, where you will be working with researchers on meaningful research problems, with access to the resources needed to pursue ambitious projects and publications. Applicants with relevant publications in these fields are highly encouraged to apply.

The Vision
We envision a future with robots that help people in our real environments with interactions that allow robots to understand, adapt, and grow with us. We believe that robots should and will work well alongside people: helping where wanted, and ultimately enabling people to spend more time on the activities they enjoy most. To achieve this, robots need to be able to operate reliably in messy, unstructured environments. We must also create robots that people can understand, collaborate with, and rely on.
 
The Team
Our team has deep cross-functional expertise across hardware, simulation, perception, controls, and machine learning. We measure our success in terms of fundamental capabilities development, as well as research impact via open-source software and publications. Come join us and let’s make general-purpose robots a reality.
 
Some of our ongoing work is highlighted here.
 
The Opportunity
We’re looking for a driven researcher with a “make it happen” mentality. The ideal candidate is able to operate independently when needed, but works well as part of a larger integrated group at the cutting edge of state-of-the-art robotics and machine learning.

Our goal is to revolutionize the field of robotics, enabling long-horizon dexterous behaviors to be efficiently taught, learned, and improved over time in diverse, real-world environments with people.

We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Researcher to join us in developing a state-of-the-art, pixels-to-action, end-to-end system for automated driving. candidates.employer_name: Toyota Research Institute (Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery)
candidates.title: Senior Research Engineer, Computer Vision (LFV/WFM)
candidates.desc:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.


The Learning From Videos (LFV) team develops world foundation models that leverage large-scale multi-modal data (RGB, depth, flow, semantics, actions, tactile, audio, etc.) from multiple domains to power downstream embodied AI tasks. Our topics of interest include Video Generation, World Models, 4D Reconstruction, Multi-Modal Models, Multi-View Geometry, Data Augmentation, and Video-Language-Action models, with a primary focus on embodied applications such as robotics and driving. We are making progress on some of the hardest scientific challenges around spatio-temporal reasoning, and how it can lead to the deployment of autonomous agents in real-world unstructured environments.
 
Our team is looking for a Research Engineer to help develop and deploy our world foundation models (WFMs) toward their key milestones in the autonomous driving domain. As our WFMs scale in both capability and ambition, we need a strong engineer who can bridge the gap between research ideas and production-grade systems. This is not a traditional software engineering role; you will work directly alongside research scientists, understand the research deeply enough to make independent technical decisions, and play a key role in enabling the deployment of key research breakthroughs into close-to-production environments.
 
As a Research Engineer, you will be responsible for supporting and optimizing large-scale distributed training of diffusion and transformer models; maintaining the infrastructure that ingests, unifies, and serves heterogeneous multi-modal datasets at scale; and developing tools and pipelines that accelerate the research-to-results cycle. You will work closely with researchers to prototype new ideas, run experiments, and help ship our most successful models toward real-world applications with real-world impact.
This role requires close collaboration with multiple TRI divisions (Robotics, Automated Driving, Human-Interactive Driving, etc.) as well external Toyota and University partners, and the ability to reconcile and prioritize possibly competing requirements in a fast-paced combination of research and production environments.

candidates.title: Technologist R&D Engineer — Optical Design & Computational Photonics
candidates.desc: The next era of intelligent systems will require entirely new approaches to photonic device design, optical architectures, simulation, and system integration. Solving these problems demands deep physical intuition, advanced computational modeling, and the ability to bridge simulation with experimental reality. We are looking for a Principal R&D Engineer to lead advanced optical design and computational photonics development for next-generation semiconductor and photonic systems. This role combines: optical simulation, inverse design, electro-thermal modeling, computational optimization, experimental interpretation, and system-level co-development. You will define and drive the optical architecture behind advanced device platforms and work across multidisciplinary teams spanning device physics, packaging, process development, characterization, and system integration. What you’ll be doing: Lead advanced optical and multiphysics simulation activities for next-generation photonic systems. Develop inverse-design and optimization methodologies for complex optical structures. Build scalable computational frameworks spanning optics, thermal, and electrical domains. Drive architecture-level tradeoff studies and system-level optical design decisions. Collaborate closely with characterization teams to correlate simulations with experimental measurements. Support co-development between devices, packaging, thermal systems, and photonic integration platforms. Develop reduced-order analytical models alongside full numerical simulation workflows. Mentor engineers and provide technical leadership across optical design and simulation activities. Help define future AI-assisted computational photonics workflows and design infrastructure. What we need to see: PhD or equivalent experience in Physics, Photonics, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or related field. 8+ years experience in optical design, computational photonics, or advanced device simulation. Strong background in optical simulation and numerical modeling. Experience with electromagnetic, optical, thermal, or multiphysics simulation tools. Strong programming capability in Python, MATLAB, or scientific computing environments. Ability to connect theoretical modeling with experimental validation and engineering constraints. Strong technical leadership and communication skills. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience with inverse design or optimization algorithms. Experience with semiconductor or integrated photonic devices. Strong multiphysics modeling capability. AI/ML-assisted simulation or optimization experience. Experience bridging device-level and system-level optical design. Demonstrated ability to solve difficult first-principles engineering problems.

Zusammenarbeit mit IT Security, um Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsanforderungen frühzeitig zu berücksichtigen und alle Lösungen entsprechend abzusichern. Unterstützung bei der Übergabe von erfolgreichen Prototypen an IT- und Entwicklungsteams für die Weiterentwicklung und Skalierung. Trendbeobachtung und Innovation: Aktive Auseinandersetzung mit aktuellen Trends und Entwicklungen im Bereich AI (Trend Radar). Identifikation neuer Technologien und Ansätze, die für ZEISS relevant sein könnten, und Bewertung ihres Potenzials für die Organisation. Messbare Ergebnisse: Dokumentation und Kommunikation der Ergebnisse von Pilotprojekten anhand von KPIs wie Zeitersparnis, Prozessverbesserungen und Innovationspotenzial. Ihr Profil Universitätsabschluss in Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung. Mindestens 5 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung in der Entwicklung und Integration von Softwarelösungen, davon mindestens 2 Jahre Erfahrung mit modernen AI-Systemen (z. B. Generative AI, LLMs, Agentic AI). Erfahrung in der schnellen Prototypisierung und im Aufbau von agentenbasierten AI-Anwendungen. Nachweisbare Fähigkeit, AI-Technologien in einem unternehmerischen Kontext zu bewerten und deren Potenziale zu demonstrieren. Technologische Kompetenzen: Fundierte Kenntnisse in Python für die AI-Entwicklung sowie Verständnis von .NET/C# Schnittstellen zur Systemintegration. Erfahrung mit Agentic Frameworks und Orchestrierungstools wie LangChain (LangGraph), Microsoft Semantic Kernel oder AutoGen. Kompetenz im Umgang mit LLMs, sowohl Cloud-basiert (z. B. Azure OpenAI) als auch On-Premise/Local (z. B. mittels vLLM, Ollama, Hugging Face) praktische Erfahrung mit RAG-Architekturen (Retrieval Augmented Generation) und Vektordatenbanken (z. B. Qdrant, Azure AI Search). Vertrautheit mit API-Entwicklung (z. B. FastAPI) und Containerisierung (Docker) zur Bereitstellung funktionaler Prototypen. Persönliche Fähigkeiten: Fähigkeit, komplexe technische Konzepte verständlich für verschiedene Zielgruppen aufzubereit
